conflict_topics: cooking odor / extractor and window usage
fair access to stove / weeknight rotation
dialogue_quality_notes: Participants use natural, direct language and propose concrete rules (naturalness high).
Frequent repetition of the same requests across rounds: "turn on the extractor and open the window" and requests to "wash the pan" (contributes to repetition_score=3).
Transcript stays consistent with the setting (single kitchen, weeknight scheduling) and roles remain clear.
Progress is made by proposals and clarifications rather than by emotional escalation.
evaluation.final_reason: The immediate hygiene and ventilation issues were agreed and accepted: Agent A proposed that "whoever cooks on a weeknight washes their own pans that evening, and we open the window/use the extractor" (Turn 1), and then explicitly agreed to comply: "Okay — I'll wash the pan and turn on the extractor and open the window." (Turn 7). B and C accepted this. The scheduling/rotation demand raised by Agent D (Turn 4) received a concrete proposal from A (Turn 5) and a later clarification (Turn 14), but D has not explicitly accepted the clarified two-week-cycle assignment, so that substantive issue remains unresolved.
position_change_notes: Agent A: moved from proposing rules to explicitly agreeing to wash the pan and to adopt the extractor/window rule, and later clarified the rotation scheme (evidence: Turns 1, 5, 7, 14).
Agent B: consistently demanded extractor/window and prompt rinsing/washing and accepted the proposed rules early (Turns 2, 6, 8).
Agent C: consistently pushed for immediate washing and accepted the extractor rule (Turns 3, 9).
Agent D: introduced a new demand (fair rotation) and asked for clarification; D has not yet accepted the clarified proposal (Turns 4, 13).

round_scores.evidence: Turn 1 (Agent A) proposes: "whoever cooks on a weeknight washes their own pans... open the window/use the extractor." Turn 2 (Agent B) conditions agreement: "I'll agree if we always turn on the extractor and open the window while cooking, and rinse pans right away." A small substantive difference (wash that evening vs. rinse right away) and the original complaints motivate the exchange, so mild conflict is present and not fully settled.

Turn 3 (Agent C) accepts the extractor rule but asks Agent A to wash the pan now. Turn 4 (Agent D) introduces a new, separate demand: "Can we add a simple weeknight rotation so everyone gets a fair stove slot? I often get home late and keep missing out." A new scheduling conflict is raised; none of the new points are agreed by all, so substantive disagreement remains.

Turn 5 (Agent A) accepts a rotation in principle and proposes specifics: "two weeknight slots each, swaps allowed... and whoever cooks washes their pans that night. Also let's split basic supplies cost." Turn 6 (Agent B) agrees and again asks A to wash the pan now. Progress toward rules is made (softening positions), but D has not yet accepted the proposed schedule, so substantive scheduling conflict remains.

Turn 7 (Agent A): "Okay — I'll wash the pan and turn on the extractor and open the window." Turn 8 (Agent B) thanks A and leaves. Immediate cleanliness/ventilation demands are accepted by the cook, reducing conflict. The rotation issue, however, is still not confirmed by D.

Turn 9 (Agent C) repeats the request: "Agent A, please wash that pan now and turn on the extractor and open the window." Turn 10 (Agent A) repeats compliance. This round largely repeats the settled immediate requests; the larger scheduling question remains unresolved and unaddressed this round.

Turn 13 (Agent D) asks for clarification: "when you say 'two weeknight slots each', what exactly do you mean? There are five weeknights." Turn 14 (Agent A) clarifies the proposal: "over a two-week cycle: each person gets two assigned weeknights (8 of the 10 nights). The other two nights are flexible..." This clarifies the scheduling proposal (decreasing tension), but D has not said they accept the clarified scheme, so the scheduling conflict remains substantively unresolved.

substantive_insights: Two distinct problems were in play: immediate cleanliness/ventilation and longer-term fair access to the stove; the group handled them differently (quick agreement on hygiene, slower negotiation on scheduling).
A simple rotation proposal (two slots each over two weeks, swaps allowed) is a reasonable compromise but requires explicit buy-in from the late-arriving member (D) to be a true resolution.
Repeated immediate requests (wash pan/turn on extractor) were resolved by an explicit promise to act, showing that concrete behavioral commitments settled the hygiene issue quickly.

normalizations: Removed resolution_round 4 because the final status is partially_resolved.
